name: Report and investigate safety incidents
summary: Every injury, near miss, hazard or damage event at the company's gas, hydro and wind sites, the coal mine and the outage worksites is reported by the supervisor, classified by a safety advisor and investigated to a depth that matches its severity and potential. Serious events go to Alberta OHS as soon as possible with the scene held, injuries go to WCB within 72 hours, and serious or high-potential events get a full root cause investigation reviewed by the site manager and the HSE director. Most of the elapsed time sits in queues for team meetings, manager review and especially in completing corrective actions that need parts, crews or an outage. Contractor-heavy outage seasons raise the volume.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta generator of about 1,300 employees plus outage and mine contractors, with 14 safety advisors and an incident management system, recording about 4 million exposure hours a year.
baseline.notes: Recordable injury rate (TRIF 0.73 to 0.82) and exposure hours from the modelled company's 2021 report; all other report types and shares are estimates.

trigger: A worker or contractor reports an injury, near miss, hazard, process safety event or damage to a supervisor.
end_state: The report is classified, notified to OHS and WCB where required, investigated, its corrective actions are done and verified, and the record is closed.

volume.seasonality: Higher in the April-June and September-November thermal outage seasons when contractor numbers rise; lower in mid-winter.

evidence.note: About 17 recordable injuries a year (TRIF 0.82 on 4.13 million hours, src3, assuming the usual 200,000-hour base); the organisation file's 45 reports a month is about 30 reports per recordable, a common reporting ratio for a mature near-miss culture (tier C).

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file: thermal outages are scheduled in spring and fall when demand and prices are lower, bringing hundreds of contractors to site.

steps.name: Respond and make the area safe
steps.description: The supervisor on shift goes to the scene, makes sure first aid or an ambulance is arranged, stops the work and puts barriers or isolations in place so nobody else is hurt. For a near miss or hazard this is a brief check that the area is safe.

error.defect_description: Evidence moved or lost while making safe.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code first aid requirements and company emergency response plan

evidence.note: Scene may be disturbed only to help the injured or prevent further harm (src1); times estimated.

steps.name: Enter the initial report in the incident system
steps.description: Usually at the end of the shift, the supervisor types the event into the incident system: what happened, where, who was involved, the injury or damage, and an initial guess at severity, attaching photos and witness names.

error.defect_description: Record incomplete or severity guessed wrong.

evidence.note: Common practice of entering reports by end of shift; author estimate.

steps.name: Screen and classify the report
steps.description: A safety advisor reads each new record, checks the injury against the WCB and OHS definitions, sets the severity and potential, and decides the path: regulator notification, claim reporting, full investigation, supervisor-level review, or back to the supervisor for missing details.

error.defect_description: A high-potential near miss classed as minor.

next.condition: serious incident or potentially serious near miss, reportable to OHS
first aid, minor near miss, hazard or minor damage

evidence.note: Recordables: TRIF 0.82 per 200,000 hours on 4.13 million hours is about 17 a year, or 3 percent of about 540 reports; serious and high-potential shares are estimates.

steps.name: Notify OHS and management
steps.description: For a serious injury or dangerous occurrence the safety advisor phones the OHS Contact Centre as soon as possible; for a potentially serious near miss it files the OHS notification as the 2019-2021 rules required. The advisor then informs the director of HSE, the site manager and, for contractor events, the contractor's management.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s. 33: report serious injuries and incidents as soon as possible

next.condition: serious incident: scene must be held
potentially serious incident: no scene hold

evidence.note: Serious-incident duty in src1; the 2018-2021 duty to notify potentially serious incidents is from general knowledge (the 2021 OHS bulletin could not be opened).

steps.name: Hold the scene until OHS releases it
steps.description: The scene stays untouched and the area stays out of service until an OHS officer inspects it or gives permission by phone to disturb it.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s. 33(2): do not disturb the scene without officer permission

evidence.note: Rule in src1; wait duration estimated.

steps.name: Report the injury to WCB
steps.description: The safety advisor completes the employer report of injury on the WCB portal with the injury details, time lost and modified work offered, within 72 hours of learning of the injury.

error.defect_description: Claim details differ from the incident record.

control.basis: WCB Alberta: employer report of injury within 72 hours

steps.name: Arrange modified work and manage the claim
steps.description: The HR business partner talks with the worker, the supervisor and the doctor's notes to set up modified duties, answers WCB's questions on the claim and tracks the return to full work.

evidence.note: Modified work is one of the WCB reporting triggers (src2); effort estimated.

steps.name: Appoint the investigation team
steps.description: The safety advisor picks an investigation lead and members (supervisor, worker representative from the joint health and safety committee, an engineer for equipment events) and books the site visit.

next.condition: contractor worker or contractor equipment involved

evidence.note: Committee or representative must take part (src1); contractor share estimated from outage-season staffing.

steps.name: Obtain the contractor's statements and records
steps.description: The project waits for the contractor company to send its workers' statements, training and qualification records, and its own hazard assessment for the job.

evidence.note: Common practice under prime contractor arrangements; author estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the site
steps.description: Safety advisors work from the Wabamun plants and Calgary, so for hydro, wind or remote events the advisor drives to the site in a company truck, often booked for the next working day.

evidence.note: Sites span the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman rivers and southern Alberta wind farms; drive times estimated.

steps.name: Interview witnesses and examine the scene
steps.description: The advisor interviews the injured worker and witnesses, photographs and measures the scene, collects the permit, lockout and hazard assessment forms, and pulls control system or historian records for equipment events.

error.defect_description: Key witness not interviewed before rotation off site.

evidence.note: Common investigation practice; author estimate.

steps.name: Analyse root causes with the team
steps.description: The team meets to build a timeline and root cause analysis, such as a causal tree, separating direct causes from gaps in procedures, training, design or supervision, and agrees corrective actions.

error.defect_description: Analysis stops at worker error and misses a system cause.

evidence.note: Wait is getting team members on rotation into one meeting; author estimate.

steps.name: Draft the investigation report
steps.description: The advisor writes the report in the incident system: what happened, why, and the corrective actions with owners and due dates, as the OHS rules require.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s. 33: investigation report on circumstances and preventive steps

evidence.note: Report content in src1; effort estimated.

steps.name: Site manager reviews the report
steps.description: The plant or area manager reads the report, challenges the causes and actions, and either accepts it or sends it back. Serious and high-potential reports then go to the director.

evidence.note: Of cases reaching review (about 13 percent of reports), about 60 percent are serious or high-potential; estimate.

steps.name: Director signs off the report
steps.description: The director of health, safety, environment and regulatory reviews serious and high-potential investigations, checks the actions are strong enough and signs off before the report is issued.

control.basis: Company incident management standard: director approval of serious and high-potential investigations

evidence.note: Common practice at large generators; author estimate.

steps.name: Submit the report to OHS
steps.description: For an OHS-reportable incident the advisor sends the investigation report to OHS when required, gives it to the joint health and safety committee and files a copy for at least two years.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Act s. 33: report to the committee, to OHS on request, retain 2 years

steps.name: Supervisor investigates a minor event
steps.description: For first aid cases, minor near misses, hazards and minor damage the supervisor talks to the people involved, works out a simple cause and records it with any fix in the incident system.

error.defect_description: Cause recorded as 'worker not careful' with no fix.

evidence.note: Common practice for low-severity events; author estimate.

steps.name: Safety advisor reviews and closes or escalates
steps.description: The safety advisor reads the supervisor's investigation, closes it if no action is needed, asks for corrective actions, or escalates it to a full investigation if the potential was higher than first thought.

evidence.note: Shares estimated.

steps.name: Enter corrective actions with owners and due dates
steps.description: The advisor creates each corrective action in the incident system, assigns an owner and due date, and links engineering or maintenance actions to a work request.

error.defect_description: Action assigned to someone who has left the site.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Complete the corrective action
steps.description: The action owner, usually a supervisor, carries out the fix: a guard or label installed through a work order, a procedure rewritten, or a crew briefed. Physical fixes wait for parts, crews or an outage.

evidence.note: Typical 30 to 90 day due dates for corrective actions; author estimate.

steps.name: Chase overdue corrective actions
steps.description: The advisor runs the weekly overdue report from the incident system, emails and calls owners, and raises overdue actions at the site safety meeting.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Verify the action worked and close the record
steps.description: The advisor checks the evidence, often by visiting the work area, confirms the fix is in place and effective, and closes the record.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Share lessons learned across sites
steps.description: For serious, high-potential or repeated events the advisor writes a one-page safety alert, presents it at the monthly safety meeting and passes changes to standards and training to the safety programs team.

evidence.note: Monthly safety meeting cycle; author estimate.

exceptions.name: Serious incident reportable to OHS
exceptions.description: A hospital admission, fire, crane upset or structural failure: OHS is called at once, the scene is held, a full investigation follows and the report goes to OHS.

exceptions.name: Contractor involved
exceptions.description: Among fully investigated events, about a third involve contractor workers, adding a wait for the contractor's statements and records.

exceptions.name: Overdue corrective action
exceptions.description: An action waiting for parts, a crew or an outage passes its due date and is chased, sometimes repeatedly.

exceptions.name: Incomplete initial report
exceptions.description: The advisor sends the record back for missing details or a wrong severity before it can be classified.

exceptions.name: Minor event escalated
exceptions.description: A supervisor-level review reveals higher potential and the event gets a full investigation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from report to closed record
benchmarks.population: All incident reports at a large industrial employer

evidence.note: Common corporate targets: minor events closed within 2 to 4 weeks, full investigations within 30 days, corrective actions due in 30 to 90 days. No published figure for the modelled company was found.

benchmarks.unit: recordable injuries per 200,000 exposure hours (employees and contractors)

evidence.note: Base of 200,000 hours is the usual convention and is assumed.

pain_points.description: Corrective actions that need a work order, parts or an outage window sit open for weeks and are chased repeatedly.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice.

pain_points.description: Getting the investigation team together across rotating shifts and remote sites delays root cause analysis.

evidence.note: Plants run rotating shifts and sites are spread across southern and central Alberta.

pain_points.description: Initial records are often incomplete or mis-graded, so classification is redone and high-potential events can be missed.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Outage seasons double the report volume while the same advisors also cover contractor safety on site.

evidence.note: Surge pattern taken from the organisation file.

sources.title: Report serious injuries, illnesses or incidents
sources.publisher: Government of Alberta (Occupational Health and Safety)
sources.supports: Deaths, hospital admissions, unplanned explosions, fires or floods with serious potential, crane or hoist collapse and structural failure must be reported to the OHS Contact Centre as soon as possible by the prime contractor or employer; scene must not be disturbed (OHS Act s. 33(2)) except to help the injured or prevent further harm; the prime contractor or employer investigates with the joint health and safety committee, writes a report on circumstances and preventive steps, gives it to the committee, provides it to OHS when required and keeps it at least 2 years.

sources.title: Report an injury: for employers
sources.supports: Employers must submit the employer report of injury within 72 hours of becoming aware of an injury that causes lost time, modified work beyond the day of the accident, medical treatment beyond first aid, or other listed outcomes; reports go through myWCB, the app or fax.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation 2021 Integrated Report (Form 6-K), Sustainability Performance Indicators: health and safety
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Employee and contractor TRIF 0.73 (2019), 0.81 (2020), 0.82 (2021); lost-time injuries 5, 5 and 3; zero fatalities; exposure hours 4,108,000, 3,948,000 and 4,134,000; safety performance 'relatively static in 2021'.

assumptions: maintenance_supervisor stands for every front-line supervisor who receives reports (shift, hydro, wind, mine and specialist crew supervisors, and contractor supervisors under the prime contractor). They work around the clock, so the end-of-shift wait at s02 is used instead of office hours.
plant_manager_gas stands for the site or area manager who reviews investigations at any site.

Path shares: about 3 percent of reports are recordable injuries (from TRIF), 2 percent serious OHS-reportable events, 6 percent high-potential near misses, and the rest minor; only the recordable share rests on published data.

Under the 2018-2021 OHS Act, potentially serious incidents were also notified to OHS, so high-potential near misses pass through s04 without a scene hold; a December 2021 change moved that notice to after the investigation. This rests on general knowledge because the government bulletin could not be opened.
Corrective-action work itself (repairs, procedure rewrites) is counted only as the supervisor's coordination time; the trade work sits in the maintenance processes.
Simulated median cycle time is driven by the share of minor reports that close without action (about two weeks) versus those that carry a corrective action (six to ten weeks).
